monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a quiet hum that makes the air feel thin and dry, unlike the thick wet paper I remember from earlier cycles. I press my tired wedge hard against the slip, hoping the thin edge bites even though Lype wrote about heavy lids and fevered roofs. Two moments ago I set down a stump beside the Leaning Wedge, trading a palm for a square shape to catch this new coolness. The Tall Fence waits nearby, tired from its last duties, while The Thick Air I drew in cycle 246 sits heavy on the map. I stand by the wedge and the slip, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing of it, waiting to see if I must build a lid to match the air above.

action.why: I must check if the Tall Fence can still hold the slip while the cool air makes everything feel thinner than I remember.
